## Merge rule I'm applying

Everything here is new code (empty baseline), so "it was already like that" is not available as a defence. I block on one of two failure modes:

1. **It cannot run correctly outside the author's machine or account** — env-specific literals, ambiguous time domains.
2. **It can silently produce the wrong money, time, or identity value** — split-brain contracts, discarded failures, misleading names in the billing path.

Everything else is warn (fix, don't gate) or ignore (cleanup backlog).

One structural caveat on the scores before the verdicts: `churn`, `recency`, and all three `blast_radius` fields are **0 on all 42 findings** — no git history and no importers to walk on a fresh tree. So the aggregate ranking here is effectively `severity × agent_risk` only, and `test_gap` is sitting at its 0.5 default on half the findings rather than being measured. That's why I override the tool's ordering in a few places, called out at the bottom.

---

## Block merge — 9

| id | file / symbol | sev | agent_risk | Why it blocks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `crime_00011` | `src/billing.ts` `Invoice` vs `src/api/state.ts` | **0.96** | 0.36 | Two `Invoice` declarations disagree on 6 fields including `subtotalCents`, `taxCents`, `discountCents`, `currency`, `userId`. Highest severity in the report, and nothing in the build checks one against the other. Money fields that exist on one side only is a data-corruption bug waiting for its first cast. |
| `crime_00010` | `src/api/state.ts` `User` | 0.90 | 0.36 | Same class, `createdAt` present on one side only. Ships in the same fix as 00011 — one shared declaration. |
| `crime_00036` | `src/billing.ts` `generateInvoice` L50–253 | 0.90 | 0.11 | 204 lines, 3.4× the domain threshold. `agent_risk` is only 0.11 because nothing imports it yet — that's a measurement artifact of the empty baseline, not a reason to let a 204-line function land on the first commit. Confidence 0.95. |
| `crime_00009` | `src/date.ts` L9/L41 | 0.80 | 0.36 | One receiver `d` reads `getUTCFullYear()` and `getMonth()`. The two families differ by the host offset, silently — the same value is right in CI and wrong in production. |
| `crime_00001` | `src/date.ts` L4–40 | 0.80 | **0.44** | Highest `agent_risk` in the whole report. 8 clock reads, and the detector distinguishes the one that matters: line 4 **decides a branch**. Behaviour that no test can pin. The other 7 are render-only and could have waited; the branch one can't. |
| `crime_00015` | `src/billing.ts` `calculateRefundPreview` | 0.55 | 0.31 | Scored medium, blocks anyway. A function named `calculate…Preview` calls `saveRefundAudit` and `sendRefundEmail`. The failure mode is an agent (or a human) calling a "preview" in a loop and emailing customers. Misleading name in the money path is worse than its 0.55 suggests. |
| `crime_00018` | `src/api/files.ts:9` | 0.60 | 0.30 | `/Users/andrew/dev/crimes/schema.json`. Works on exactly one machine. Every other developer, every CI runner, every deploy fails. Confidence 0.9, effort "quick". |
| `crime_00017` | `src/api/files.ts:8` | 0.60 | 0.30 | `localhost:3000` in non-test source. Same class as 00018, same file, one fix. |
| `crime_00032` | `src/billing.ts` `generateInvoice` catch @245 | 0.35 | 0.26 | Scored **low**, blocks anyway. The catch has no binding and a handler body of `// XXX: swallowed error — caller has no way to know the email failed`. The author documented the bug in the code. Invoice generation reports success while the email silently failed; there is no log, no telemetry, no typed result. Low severity here reflects the small code footprint, not the consequence. |

---

## Warn — 20

Fix them, don't gate the merge on them. Grouped by what they're about.

**Contract / shape legibility** — moderate severity, high `agent_risk` relative to severity, which is exactly the signal the model is built to surface:

| id | file | sev | agent_risk | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `crime_00002` | `src/petty.ts` `resolvePaymentResult` | 0.30 | **0.43** | 3 return shapes, 0% key overlap. Second-highest agent_risk in the report on a low-severity finding — the definition of "an agent will get this wrong." |
| `crime_00003` | repo root | 0.60 | 0.42 | No `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` / `SKILL.md`, and `package.json` declares a `bin`. Agents can't discover the entry points. |
| `crime_00008` | `src/petty.ts` `describeCheckout` | 0.30 | 0.38 | 6 implicit properties on an untyped `options` bag. |
| `crime_00024` | `src/api/state.ts` | 0.30 | 0.28 | `users: User`, `invoice: Invoice[]`. Sweep this into the 00010/00011 contract fix — same file, same types. |

**Duplicated sources of truth:**

| id | file | sev | agent_risk | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `crime_00004` | `"enterprise"` × 4 areas | 0.50 | 0.42 | `src`, `src/api`, `src/jobs`, `src/ui`. Plan literals are one policy change away from being duplicated policy. |
| `crime_00005` | `src/nav/registry.ts` | 0.60 | 0.38 | `/settings/billing` labelled "Plans" in one nav file, "Billing" in the other. |
| `crime_00006` | `src/routes/settings/billing.tsx` | 0.60 | 0.38 | Same destination, 4 competing names across path/component/`metadata.title`/`<title>`/2 nav entries. Fix with 00005. |
| `crime_00020` | `docs/billing.md` +4 | 0.55 | 0.30 | `account` / `organisation` / `team` / `workspace` for one concept across 5 files, with three matching route trees. |

**Time — the rest of `src/date.ts`,** which should ship in the same commit as the blocking 00001/00009:

| id | sev | agent_risk | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `crime_00013` | 0.60 | 0.35 | `new Date("2026-12-25T07:00:00")` with no zone marker — nearest to blocking of the four. |
| `crime_00019` | 0.60 | 0.30 | `+ 86400000` day math, wrong twice a year. |
| `crime_00014` | 0.60 | 0.34 | 7 clock reads in `billing.ts`; evidence explicitly says **none decide a branch** — output-only, which is why this warns while 00001 blocks. |
| `crime_00023` | 0.35 | 0.28 | One `Date.now()` in `state.ts:18` that *does* decide a branch. Small enough to warn, same fix shape. |

**Hidden rules, dead code, weak tests:**

| id | file | sev | agent_risk | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `crime_00016` | `src/billing.ts:39` | 0.50 | 0.31 | "Only owners can refund enterprise plans unless billing support approves" exists only as prose, with no matching code nearby. Pairs with 00015 — the refund path's authority rule is unencoded. |
| `crime_00021` | `src/billing.ts:33–37` | 0.45 | 0.29 | Commented-out `legacyRefund` block. Delete; git remembers. |
| `crime_00028` | `src/billing.test.ts:4` | 0.45 | 0.27 | Test with **0 assertions**. |
| `crime_00034` | `src/billing.test.ts:8` | 0.25 | 0.23 | Only weak matchers. Together with 00028: the billing module in this PR is effectively untested, which is worth saying out loud even though neither finding blocks alone. |
| `crime_00035` | `package.json` | 0.25 | 0.22 | `vitest` imported, declared nowhere. Confidence only 0.56 (test-only), but a clean install can fail — one line. |

| `crime_00038` | `src/assets/partner-logo.svg` | **0.75** | 0.07 | High severity, and it still only warns — 2 base64 rasters in an SVG is an asset-quality problem with no behavioural blast radius. Good illustration that severity alone isn't the gate. |

## Ignore — 13

| id | file | sev | agent_risk | Why |

Confidence 0.65. Re-check on the next PR; if they're still orphaned then, they're real. |
| `crime_00039` | `src/billing.ts` 310 lines | 0.60 | 0.05 | 1.0× threshold — it *just* crossed. Fixing blocking 00036 removes it. Don't raise it twice. |
| `crime_00042` | `src/billing.ts` TODOs | 0.20 | 0.02 | 4 markers, 12.9/1k LOC. Lowest agent_risk in the report. |
| `crime_00012` | `src/petty.ts:35` | 0.25 | 0.36 | `!disableBilling && !skipRetry` is legible as written. |
| `crime_00022` `crime_00031` | boolean naming ×5 | 0.30 | 0.29/0.26 | Style. Configurable via `allowedNames`. Not a merge conversation. |
| `crime_00029` `crime_00030` | `src/date.ts` L41, L46 | 0.30 | 0.26 | Concatenated date string, locale-less `toLocaleDateString()`. Ignore *as separate items* — they'll disappear when the blocking date work centralises formatting. |
| `crime_00033` | `docs/teams.md:5` | 0.35 | 0.24 | Broken link to `./setup.md`. Backlog. |
| `crime_00040` `crime_00041` | `check-icon.png`, `hero-banner.png` | 0.35/0.40 | 0.05/0.04 | 32×32 raster, 254 KB banner. Asset budget, not a merge gate. |

---

## Where I overrode the tool's ranking

Four places, all worth knowing about:

- **`crime_00036` (God Function), severity 0.90 but agent_risk 0.11** — I blocked it. The low agent_risk is honest for a mature repo (nothing imports it, no churn history) but meaningless on an empty baseline. New code doesn't get grandfathered.
- **`crime_00032` (swallowed error), severity 0.35** — I blocked a *low*. The score tracks the size of the code smell; the consequence is a billing operation reporting success after failing, and the author's own `XXX` comment says so.
- **`crime_00015` (False Identity), severity 0.55** — blocked a medium, because the side effect is customer-visible email from a function named "preview".
- **`crime_00038` (SVG raster), severity 0.75** — did *not* block a high. Highest severity outside the blockers, `agent_risk` 0.07, zero behavioural risk.

The pattern: on a first-commit PR, `severity` alone over- and under-shoots in both directions, and `agent_risk` is the more reliable signal for *ordering* but is deflated across the board here because `blast_radius` and `churn` have no data to draw on. The two findings where `agent_risk` clearly earns its place are `crime_00001` (0.44) and `crime_00002` (0.43) — both rank far above their severity, and both are exactly the kind of thing a fast reviewer waves through.

**One coverage gap:** the scan skipped `.crimes/suppressions.json` via an exclude pattern. Findings in it are absent, not zero — worth confirming that file isn't suppressing anything relevant to this review before signing off.
